subject: Chains finding different, but symmetrical maximums

messages.author: dc34e6802c30b23a
messages.subject: Chains finding different, but symmetrical maximums
parts:
(Sorry if this has been asked and answered; I wasn't sure what it's called and so what to search for.)

Running the following in R, I get output that suggests some chains have found one maximum, and others have found a different but symmetrical maximum: http://i.imgur.com/NjpBHEp.jpg.  The estimates for mu and sigma are similarly bifurcated.

Is there any way to constrain my parameters such that theta[1] < theta[2], say, or is there a better way to deal with this?

Thanks.

modelString = "
  data {
    int N;
    int K;
    real durs[N];
  }
  parameters {
    simplex[K] theta;
    real<lower=0> mu[K];
    real<lower=0> sigma[K];
  }
  model {
    real ps[K];
    sigma ~ cauchy(100, 100);
    mu ~ cauchy(100, 100);
    for (n in 1:N) {
      for (k in 1:K) {
        ps[k] = log(theta[k]) + normal_lpdf(durs[n] | mu[k], sigma[k]);
      }
      target += log_sum_exp(ps);
    }
  }
"
dso = stan_model(model_code=modelString)

N <- 1000
comps <- sample(1:2,prob=c(.8, .2), size=N, replace=TRUE)
mus <- c(50, 150)
sds <- c(10, 100)
duration <- rnorm(n=N, mean=mus[comps], sd=sds[comps])

data <- list(N=length(duration), durs=duration, K=2)
out <- sampling(object=dso, data=data, chains=10)
plot(out, pars='theta', plotfun='hist')

messages.subject: Re: Chains finding different, but symmetrical maximums
parts:
On Thursday, December 8, 2016 at 1:27:43 PM UTC-5, Toby Burress wrote:
Running the following in R, I get output that suggests some chains have found one maximum, and others have found a different but symmetrical maximum: http://i.imgur.com/NjpBHEp.jpg.  The estimates for mu and sigma are similarly bifurcated.

Is there any way to constrain my parameters such that theta[1] < theta[2], say, or is there a better way to deal with this?

The least bad approach is usually to make mu (positive) ordered via

parameters {
  simplex[K] theta;
  positive_ordered[K] mu;
  real<lower=0> sigma[K];
}

But cauchy(100,100) priors almost never make sense in a Stan program.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Chains finding different, but symmetrical maximums
parts:
It's usually called the "label switching" problem, which is
a kind of multimodality, and in this case, a specific kind
of non-identifiability. So there are lots of places to look.

- Bob
